titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto:
People have the right to be involved in discussions and make informed decisions about their care, as described in NICE's information about shared decision making.

Making decisions using NICE guidelines explains how we use words to show the strength (or certainty) of our recommendations, and has information about prescribing medicines (including off‑label use), professional guidelines, standards and laws (including on consent and mental capacity), and safeguarding.

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto:
Think about alternative diagnoses when examining or reviewing people with low back pain, particularly if they develop new or changed symptoms. Exclude specific causes of low back pain, for example, cancer, infection, trauma or inflammatory disease such as spondyloarthritis. If serious underlying pathology is suspected, refer to relevant NICE guidelines on:

- metastatic spinal cord compression in adults - spinal injury - spondyloarthritis in over 16s - suspected cancer. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider using risk stratification (for example, the STarT Back risk assessment tool) at first point of contact with a healthcare professional for each new episode of low back pain with or without sciatica to inform shared decision-making about stratified management. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto:
Based on risk stratification, consider:

- simpler and less intensive support for people with low back pain with or without sciatica likely to improve quickly and have a good outcome (for example, reassurance, advice to keep active and guidance on self-management) - more complex and intensive support for people with low back pain with or without sciatica at higher risk of a poor outcome (for example, exercise programmes with or without manual therapy). [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not routinely offer imaging in a non-specialist setting for people with low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Explain to people with low back pain with or without sciatica that if they are being referred for specialist opinion, they may not need imaging. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider imaging in specialist settings of care (for example, a musculoskeletal interface clinic or hospital) for people with low back pain with or without sciatica only if the result is likely to change management. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto:
Provide people with advice and information, tailored to their needs and capabilities, to help them self-manage their low back pain with or without sciatica, at all steps of the treatment pathway. Include:

- information on the nature of low back pain and sciatica - encouragement to continue with normal activities. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider a group exercise programme (biomechanical, aerobic, mind–body or a combination of approaches) within the NHS for people with a specific episode or flare-up of low back pain with or without sciatica. Take people's specific needs, preferences and capabilities into account when choosing the type of exercise. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer belts or corsets for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer foot orthotics for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer rocker sole shoes for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer traction for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider manual therapy (spinal manipulation, mobilisation or soft tissue techniques such as massage) for managing low back pain with or without sciatica, but only as part of a treatment package that includes exercise. [2016, amended 2026]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer acupuncture for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer ultrasound for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer percutaneous electrical nerve simulation (PENS) for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer transcutaneous electrical nerve simulation (TENS) for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer interferential therapy for managing low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: NICE removed this recommendation in July 2026 because a surveillance review found that this recommendation may be out of date, but an update was not prioritised in this area.

instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: NICE removed this recommendation in July 2026 because a surveillance review found that this recommendation may be out of date, but an update was not prioritised in this area.

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Promote and facilitate return to work or normal activities of daily living for people with low back pain with or without sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer gabapentinoids, other antiepileptics, oral corticosteroids or benzodiazepines for managing sciatica as there is no overall evidence of benefit and there is evidence of harm. [2020]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: If a person is already taking opioids, gabapentinoids or benzodiazepines for sciatica, explain the risks of continuing these medicines. See also the section on reviewing medicines in NICE's guideline on medicines associated with dependence or withdrawal symptoms. [2020]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto:
As part of shared decision making about whether to stop opioids, gabapentinoids or benzodiazepines for sciatica, discuss the problems associated with withdrawal with the person.

To support discussions with patients about the benefits and harms of these treatment, and safe withdrawal management, see:

- NICE's guideline on medicines associated with dependence or withdrawal symptoms - NICE's guideline on shared decision making - the section on medication review in NICE's guideline on medicines optimisation. [2020].

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Be aware of the risk of harms and limited evidence of benefit from the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) in sciatica. [2020]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto:
If prescribing NSAIDs for sciatica:

- take into account potential differences in gastrointestinal, liver and cardio-renal toxicity, and the person's risk factors, including age - think about appropriate clinical assessment, ongoing monitoring of risk factors, and the use of gastroprotective treatment - use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period of time. [2020]

For a short explanation of why the committee made the 2020 recommendations and how they might affect practice, see the rationale and impact section on pharmacological management of sciatica.

The committee have also made recommendations for research on opioids for the management of acute sciatica, and antidepressants for the management of sciatica.

Full details of the evidence and the committee's discussion are in evidence review A: pharmacological management of sciatica.

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider oral NSAIDs for managing low back pain, taking into account potential differences in gastrointestinal, liver and cardio-renal toxicity, and the person's risk factors, including age. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: When prescribing oral NSAIDs for low back pain, think about appropriate clinical assessment, ongoing monitoring of risk factors, and the use of gastroprotective treatment. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Prescribe oral NSAIDs for low back pain at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period of time. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider weak opioids (with or without paracetamol) for managing acute low back pain only if an NSAID is contraindicated, not tolerated or has been ineffective. For guidance on safe prescribing of opioids and managing withdrawal, see NICE's guideline on medicines associated with dependence or withdrawal symptoms. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not routinely offer opioids for managing acute low back pain (see recommendation 1.2.25). [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors or tricyclic antidepressants for managing low back pain. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer gabapentinoids or antiepileptics for managing low back pain. [2016, amended 2020]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto:
Consider referral for assessment for radiofrequency denervation for people with chronic low back pain when:

- non-surgical treatment has not worked for them and - the main source of pain is thought to come from structures supplied by the medial branch nerve and - they have moderate or severe levels of localised back pain (rated as 5 or more on a visual analogue scale, or equivalent) at the time of referral. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Only perform radiofrequency denervation in people with chronic low back pain after a positive response to a diagnostic medial branch block. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer imaging for people with low back pain with specific facet join pain as a prerequisite for radiofrequency denervation. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider epidural injections of local anaesthetic and steroid in people with acute and severe sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not use epidural injections for neurogenic claudication in people who have central spinal canal stenosis. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not allow a person's BMI, smoking status or psychological distress to influence the decision to refer them for a surgical opinion for sciatica. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Consider spinal decompression for people with sciatica when non-surgical treatment has not improved pain or function and their radiological findings are consistent with sciatic symptoms. [2016]

titulo_fonte: Low back pain and sciatica in over 16s: assessment and management (NICE guideline NG59)
instituicoes: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
texto: Do not offer spinal fusion for people with low back pain unless as part of a randomised controlled trial. [2016]
